issues.description: Wasted NewStats call leaks a counter into the registry on every value_to_metric request
issues.detail: In the override block, NewRateLimit(...) is called with this.statsManager.NewStats(rateLimit.FullKey) and then rateLimit.Stats is immediately overwritten with NewStats(enhancedKey). The first NewStats registers a counter under the old key that is never used. On a hot GetLimit path this is both wasteful and pollutes the stats registry. Drop the NewRateLimit recreate entirely; just set Stats and FullKey.

issues.description: Enhanced key is built for entries past the matched depth, producing garbage suffixes
issues.detail: The valueToMetricFullKey builder appends a segment for every entry in descriptor.Entries, including ones where nextDescriptor is nil (no match). The fallback writes entry.Key anyway. This means partial-match descriptors silently generate a different enhancedKey from FullKey and trigger the override block with a bogus tail. Stop appending once nextDescriptor is nil, the same way the existing matching loop stops being useful.

issues.description: Bad taste: three branches with near-identical bodies instead of one
issues.detail: The matchedViaWildcard / matchedUsingValue / default-key sections all do essentially the same thing: write key, optionally write _value if entry.Value != "" and the flag is set or the match was explicit. Collapse to one decision (should we include value?) and one write. This is the textbook special-case-that-should-be-general; eliminate the special cases, do not enumerate them.

issues.description: rateLimit.FullKey is read and written but not shown to be added to RateLimit struct
issues.detail: The patch references rateLimit.FullKey in both the DetailedMetric branch and the new override block. If FullKey did not previously exist on RateLimit, this does not compile; if it did, the prior detailed-metric path was not setting it and now suddenly does, which may change downstream behavior. Either way, the struct change belongs in the diff with a one-line justification.

issues.description: Override block runs even when no value_to_metric flag is set anywhere
issues.detail: The block triggers whenever enhancedKey != rateLimit.FullKey. Because the new builder writes entry.Key segments unconditionally, any path where the original FullKey was built differently (e.g., wildcards, default-key fallbacks) can diverge and force a NewStats call on every request. Gate this on "some descriptor in the chain actually had valueToMetric=true", tracked as a bool during traversal.

issues.description: Struct literal initialization by position is fragile across future field additions
issues.detail: newDescriptor := &rateLimitDescriptor{map[string]*rateLimitDescriptor{}, rateLimit, nil, descriptorConfig.ValueToMetric} uses positional init. The next person to add a field will silently shift this and the rateLimitDomain init below. Use named fields; this is a long-lived codebase and positional literals are hostile to the next maintainer.

review.summary: Patch solves a real problem (per-runtime-value metric cardinality without going full detailed_metric), but the implementation has bad taste and at least one correctness/perf bug. The valueToMetricFullKey builder enumerates three near-identical branches that should collapse into one, and it keeps appending segments past the matched depth, producing keys that diverge from FullKey even when no value_to_metric flag is set. The recreate-then-overwrite of Stats wastes a NewStats call on every request, leaking counters into the registry. FullKey on RateLimit is read and written without showing the struct change. NEEDS-WORK: refactor the key builder, gate the override on actual flag usage, drop the wasted NewRateLimit call, and switch struct literals to named fields. The tests are thorough for the happy paths but miss the wildcard-without-flag and no-match cases that the bugs above would expose.
